newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE wheat rises, taking cue from firm French mkt.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE wheat rises, taking cue from firm French mkt.

text.p: LIFFE wheat futures rose on Monday, taking their cue from a strong French market, traders said.
As the rise gathered momentum, more buyers came into the market, giving London some follow-through, they said.
"It found a bit of support from the French early in the day and followed through, hitting technical levels. Then people wanted to have a go," one trader said.
But the higher levels brought some sellers back into the market later into the day, taking wheat off its highs.

The French physical market was steady today, after the firm end to last week which so excited London, traders there said. They did not expect active trade ahead of the holiday Friday, especially as there is no EU tender this week.
Futures were helped by firm UK physical markets, as operators struggled to find grain off farms.
Active July wheat last traded 0.75 stg higher at 104.40 stg, having seen a high of 105.50 stg earlier in the day. July volume was 292 of a total 753 lots of wheat
The main buyers were physical market traders who had found supplies off farm short and turned to the futures market, traders said.

Wheat's rise was despite a firm sterling, which gained against the mark on robust UK current account and GDP data. "Sterling was nothing to do with it," the trader said, noting that the market would probably have gone down by as much as it actually went up if traders' eyes had been on the currency.
Barley firmed in thin trade. By the close only November had traded, with 15 lots changing hands. It last traded 0.25 sterling higher at 95.25 stg.
